A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same dual-agent visual-inertial odometry framework. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete supplementary material support comparison; moved appendix content can be matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original EuRoC and TUM-VI evaluations, runtime measurements, component ablations, and visual-degradation experiments in Sections 4.2–4.5 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds sensor-degradation tests, scale-monitor comparisons, and a TUM-VI-to-EuRoC transfer result in Appendix D.

M1.justification: v2 adds an Online Scale Monitor that compares IMU and VO motion magnitudes over 15 frames and corrects persistent scale deviations. This extends the startup scale estimation in v1; the core agents, objectives, and VO backend remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish that the monitor was used in the retained benchmark results.

E1.justification: The datasets and odometry task remain unchanged. Appendix D extends the tested input conditions beyond v1's mild visual corruption to visual outages, severe blur, and increased IMU noise on EuRoC MH 04.

E2.justification: New Table 12 introduces an internal comparison between Ours (Base) and Ours (+Monitor). No external comparator is added: DPVO already appeared in the robustness comparison, and the VS-VIO evaluation in Table 10 is retained from v1.

E3.justification: Added protocols specify a 2-second blackout, blur affecting 30% of frames, doubled IMU noise, and ±20% initialization error. A separate transfer experiment fine-tunes only on TUM-VI Corridor 4 before testing EuRoC MH 04. Existing evaluation settings and Table 7 PPO hyperparameters are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix D adds focused sensor-failure tests, initialization-scale sensitivity with a monitor ablation, and one cross-dataset transfer test. These extend the existing robustness and generalization analyses; the original component ablations and mild-blur experiments remain unchanged.

E5.justification: There are no additions or revisions to repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or statistical tests. The new experiments report point estimates without introducing an uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Existing tabulated and plotted results are unchanged. New Table 11 reports outage errors of 1.928 for DPVO versus 1.114 for Ours, and severe-blur errors of 1.122 versus 0.472. Table 12 reports scale-error results of 0.661/0.682 for Base versus 0.522/0.508 with Monitor, while nominal error rises from 0.092 to 0.096. The added transfer result is 0.173 m. These are additional results, not established same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations, losses, initialization derivation, and IMU pre-integration equations are retained. The monitor is described procedurally without adding a formal derivation, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain their accuracy, efficiency, and dual-agent contribution claims. New Appendix E strengthens the novelty assertion by explicitly claiming, to the authors' knowledge, the first RL-based dynamic IMU–visual fusion framework.

C2.justification: v2 acknowledges MLP1's limited ability to correct large initial scale errors, interprets stress-test resilience through adaptive fusion, and attributes transfer degradation to IMU noise differences. It also discusses residual outage drift. The original limitations are moved unchanged to Appendix F, which still says cross-dataset transfer was not explored.

D1.justification: v2 supplies the monitor's 15-frame window and motion-ratio correction description, although its trigger threshold remains unspecified. Appendix A.2 adds training-stability explanations; the entropy coefficients, learning rates, and supervised pretraining were already documented. Hardware and resource-access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: New Appendix E expands the positioning against RL-based VO and adds an explicit first-use claim for RL-based visual-inertial fusion. Its pre-emptive gating distinction largely repeats Section 2.3. No cited work is added or removed; reference 26 only gains arXiv metadata.

P1.justification: The main narrative is essentially unchanged. v2 adds training explanations and experimental discussion, inserts Appendix E on novelty, and relabels the existing limitations as Appendix F. Other edits include table-label capitalization and bibliographic metadata.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 11 and 12, changes Table 2's emphasis and label formatting, and reflows appendix figures and tables around the added text. Existing plotted graphics are unchanged; there is no broad visual redesign.

improvement.justification: The added failure, scale-monitor, and transfer tests could strengthen empirical coverage, but inconsistencies obscure their evidential value. Table 11's nominal DPVO/Ours values are 0.106/0.092 for the stated MH 04 evaluation, whereas retained Table 6 reports 0.137/0.112, without an explained setting difference. Appendix F also denies cross-dataset evaluation despite the new transfer result. These unresolved conflicts prevent a reliable judgment of net quality improvement.
